stem: The force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact is called __________.
solution: Friction is the force that opposes motion between surfaces in contact.

stem: Friction acts in a direction __________ to the direction of motion.
solution: Friction always acts opposite to the direction in which the object moves or tends to move.

stem: Friction is caused mainly by the __________ of the surfaces in contact.
solution: Friction arises from the interlocking of irregularities on the surfaces in contact.

stem: Friction is greater between __________ surfaces.
solution: Rougher surfaces have more irregularities, so friction is greater between them.

stem: The friction acting when an object is at rest and just about to move is called __________ friction.
solution: Static friction acts on an object at rest and prevents it from starting to move until enough force is applied.

stem: The friction acting when one object slides over another is called __________ friction.
solution: Sliding (kinetic) friction acts between surfaces that are sliding over each other.

stem: The friction when an object rolls over a surface is called __________ friction.
solution: Rolling friction acts when an object rolls over a surface; it is much smaller than sliding friction.

stem: Which of the following is the smallest for the same pair of surfaces?
solution: Rolling friction is the least, which is why wheels and ball bearings are used to reduce friction.

stem: Static friction is generally __________ sliding friction.
solution: Static friction (needed to start motion) is a little greater than sliding friction (needed to keep it moving).

stem: Friction increases when the two surfaces are pressed together __________.
solution: Pressing surfaces together harder increases friction between them.

stem: The wheels of vehicles use ball bearings to reduce friction by converting sliding friction into __________ friction.
solution: Ball bearings replace sliding friction with much smaller rolling friction, reducing wear.

stem: The substances applied between two surfaces to reduce friction are called __________.
solution: Lubricants like oil and grease form a thin layer between surfaces, reducing friction.

stem: Oiling the moving parts of a machine reduces friction because the oil __________.
options: fills the irregularities and forms a smooth layer
solution: Oil fills the tiny gaps and forms a smooth layer, so the surfaces slide more easily with less friction.

stem: The soles of shoes and the tyres of vehicles are grooved to __________.
solution: Grooves (treads) increase friction/grip, preventing slipping.

stem: We are able to walk without slipping because of __________.
options: friction between our feet and the ground
solution: Friction between our feet and the ground gives the grip we need to walk without slipping.

stem: Walking on a wet or oily floor is difficult because these surfaces have __________ friction.
solution: Wet or oily floors have reduced friction, so it is easy to slip.

stem: Which of the following is a harmful effect of friction?
options: Wearing out of machine parts and shoe soles
solution: Friction wears out surfaces (machine parts, tyres, soles) and generates heat, which are harmful effects.

stem: Friction produces __________ when two surfaces rub against each other.
solution: Rubbing surfaces produce heat; e.g., rubbing hands warms them.

stem: A matchstick lights when struck because of __________.
solution: Striking a matchstick produces heat by friction, which ignites the chemicals on its head.

stem: Which of the following is a way to increase friction?
options: Making a surface rough or using treads
solution: Roughening surfaces or adding treads increases friction; polishing, oil and bearings reduce it.

stem: Which of the following reduces friction?
solution: Polishing and lubrication reduce friction between surfaces.

stem: Sportspersons use spiked shoes to __________.
solution: Spikes increase grip (friction), preventing slipping and helping athletes run better.

stem: The friction exerted by liquids and gases on objects moving through them is called __________.
solution: Fluid friction, or drag, is the resistance offered by liquids and gases to objects moving through them.

stem: Objects like aeroplanes and ships are given a __________ shape to reduce fluid friction.
solution: A streamlined shape lets fluid flow past smoothly, reducing drag (fluid friction).

stem: Fish and birds have streamlined bodies to __________.
options: reduce fluid friction as they move through water/air
solution: Streamlined bodies reduce drag, helping fish swim and birds fly with less resistance.

stem: Which of the following would experience the most friction while moving?
options: A block on a smooth glass surface
A ball rolling on a marble floor
A block on a polished floor
solution: Sandpaper is very rough, so dragging a block over it produces the most friction.

stem: Friction is sometimes called a 'necessary evil' because it __________.
options: is essential for many tasks but also causes wear and energy loss
solution: Friction is necessary (walking, gripping, braking) but also causes wear and wastes energy as heat — hence a 'necessary evil'.

stem: Brakes of a bicycle work due to __________.
options: friction between the brake pads and the wheel rim
solution: Braking presses pads against the rim, and the friction slows and stops the wheel.

stem: If there were no friction, a moving object would __________.
options: keep moving and be hard to stop
solution: Without friction, there would be nothing to slow a moving object, so it would keep moving and be hard to stop.

stem: Which of the following statements about rolling friction is TRUE?
options: It is less than sliding friction, so rolling is easier than dragging
It is more than sliding friction
It is the same as static friction
solution: Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction, which is why it is easier to roll a heavy object than to drag it.

stem: The invention of the wheel greatly helped humans because it __________.
options: reduced friction by converting sliding into rolling
solution: The wheel reduces friction by replacing sliding with rolling, making it easier to move loads.

stem: Powder (like talcum or graphite) sprinkled on a carrom board __________.
options: reduces friction so the coins slide easily
solution: The powder acts as a dry lubricant, reducing friction so the striker and coins slide smoothly.

stem: The heat generated by friction between machine parts can be reduced by __________.
solution: Lubricants reduce friction and thus the heat generated between moving machine parts.

stem: Which of the following depends on friction to work?
options: Writing with a pen or pencil on paper
solution: Writing requires friction between the pen/pencil and paper to leave a mark.

stem: The reason a car skids on a wet road is that water __________.
options: reduces the friction between the tyres and the road
solution: Water reduces the friction (grip) between the tyres and road, so the car can skid.

stem: Which of the following surfaces would give the least friction?
solution: A polished marble floor is very smooth, giving the least friction.

stem: The soles of new shoes have more grip than worn-out shoes because worn soles have __________.
solution: Worn-out soles become smooth, reducing friction (grip), so they are more slippery.

stem: Fluid friction can be reduced by giving objects a __________ shape.
solution: A streamlined shape reduces fluid friction (drag) by allowing smooth flow of the fluid.

stem: The force of friction depends on the __________ of the surfaces in contact.
options: smoothness/roughness and how hard they press
solution: Friction depends on the nature (roughness) of the surfaces and how hard they are pressed together.

stem: Ball bearings are used in machines and vehicles mainly to __________.
solution: Ball bearings reduce friction (using rolling motion), reducing wear and energy loss.

stem: Meteors burn up on entering the Earth's atmosphere due to heat produced by __________.
solution: Friction (drag) with air molecules heats up meteors so much that they burn up.

stem: Which of the following would you do to make it easier to slide a heavy box across the floor?
options: Place it on rollers or wheels
solution: Rollers or wheels convert sliding friction into smaller rolling friction, making the box easier to move.

stem: Friction between the tyre and the road is important for a moving vehicle because it __________.
options: provides grip for moving, turning and braking
solution: Tyre-road friction gives the grip needed to move, steer and brake safely.

stem: The advantage of a smooth, polished surface in a machine is that it __________.
options: reduces friction and wear of parts
solution: Smooth surfaces reduce friction, minimising wear and heat between moving parts.

stem: A gymnast applies coarse powder on their hands before performing to __________.
solution: Coarse powder increases friction, giving the gymnast a firmer grip.

stem: Which of the following is TRUE about friction?
options: It can be both useful and harmful
It has no effect on us
solution: Friction is useful (walking, gripping, braking) and harmful (wear, heat), so it is both.

stem: A rough football ground provides __________ than a smooth marble floor.
solution: A rough ground provides more friction than a smooth marble floor.

stem: Which of the following would reduce friction between two metal parts sliding over each other?
solution: Grease or oil (lubricants) form a smooth layer that reduces friction between the metal parts.

stem: Ball bearings reduce friction by replacing sliding friction with __________.
solution: Ball bearings convert sliding friction into much smaller rolling friction, reducing wear.

stem: A streamlined shape helps reduce __________.
solution: A streamlined shape reduces fluid friction (drag) as an object moves through air or water.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Friction' is that:
options: friction opposes motion, depends on surface roughness and contact force, and can be increased or decreased as needed for daily life
solution: The chapter explains friction, its types and causes, its useful and harmful effects, and ways to increase or reduce it.

stem: Friction acts in a direction __________ to the motion of an object.
solution: Friction always acts opposite to the direction of motion.

stem: Friction is greater on a __________ surface.
solution: Rough surfaces produce more friction than smooth ones.

stem: Friction is caused by the __________ between the surfaces in contact.
solution: The tiny irregularities of surfaces interlock, causing friction.

stem: The friction acting on a stationary object is called __________ friction.
solution: Static friction acts on an object at rest before it starts moving.

stem: The friction acting on a sliding object is called __________ friction.
solution: Sliding (kinetic) friction acts on an object already in motion.

stem: Sliding friction is slightly __________ than static friction.
solution: Once motion begins, sliding friction is a little less than static friction.

stem: Rolling friction is __________ than sliding friction.
solution: Rolling friction is much less than sliding friction, which is why wheels ease movement.

stem: Ball bearings reduce friction by converting sliding into __________.
solution: Ball bearings replace sliding with rolling, greatly reducing friction.

stem: A substance applied to reduce friction between surfaces is called a __________.
solution: Lubricants like oil and grease reduce friction between surfaces.

stem: The treads on tyres and shoe soles are designed to __________.
solution: Treads increase friction for a better grip, preventing slipping.

stem: Friction produces __________ when two surfaces rub together.
solution: Rubbing surfaces produce heat, which is why palms warm when rubbed.

stem: Which of the following is an advantage of friction?
solution: Friction lets us walk, write and grip objects.

stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of friction?
options: Wear and tear of machine parts
solution: Friction causes wear and tear and wastes energy as heat.

stem: The resistance offered by air to a moving object is called __________.
solution: Air resistance is a kind of friction that opposes motion through air.

stem: The resistance offered by fluids (liquids and gases) to objects moving through them is called __________.
solution: Fluid friction, or drag, opposes objects moving through liquids and gases.

stem: Streamlined shapes of fish, birds and aeroplanes help to __________.
solution: Streamlining reduces fluid friction, allowing easier, faster movement.

stem: Sportspersons wear spiked shoes to __________.
solution: Spikes increase friction, giving a firm grip so athletes do not slip.

stem: Friction can be reduced by making surfaces __________.
solution: Smoothing and polishing surfaces reduces friction.

stem: Oiling a squeaky hinge reduces the __________ between the moving parts.
solution: Oil acts as a lubricant, reducing friction and the squeak.

stem: Walking on a wet, smooth floor is difficult because friction is __________.
solution: Water reduces friction, making a smooth floor slippery.

stem: Sprinkling powder on a carrom board __________ friction.
solution: The powder reduces friction, letting the coins slide smoothly.

stem: Friction is sometimes called a __________ because it is both useful and harmful.
solution: Friction is called a 'necessary evil' as it is both useful and a nuisance.

stem: Without friction, it would be __________ to walk.
solution: Without friction we could not grip the ground, so walking would be impossible.

stem: A parachute increases __________ to slow a person's fall.
solution: A large parachute increases air resistance, slowing the descent.

stem: The main reason machine parts are lubricated is to reduce __________ and wear.
solution: Lubrication reduces friction and the resulting wear on machine parts.

stem: Wheels are used to move heavy loads because rolling friction is __________.
solution: Rolling friction is small, so wheels make moving heavy loads easier.

stem: The main cause of energy loss in machines due to friction is the production of __________.
solution: Friction converts useful energy into heat, causing energy loss in machines.
